AIM.1.description: On a host read, capture wins over clear: fault_reg is loaded with the causes live on that clock instead of being emptied
AIM.1.after: else if (fault_reg_read_done) begin /  / fault_reg <= {FAULT_CAUSE_W{convertor_running}} & {ovp, latch_assert, otp_state, uvlo_state, (window_trip || window_trip_SS)};
AIM.1.reason: A read landing while a cause is live and the converter is running leaves fault_reg non-empty on the next clock instead of zero, and because fault_reg never passes through empty, fault_time stays at 0 instead of re-latching the new episode's start time.

AIM.2.description: fault_time capture takes priority over its clear-on-read, the opposite of fault_reg
AIM.2.before: else if (fault_reg_read_done)     fault_time <= '0; / else if (episode_start)           fault_time <= timestamp_ms;
AIM.2.after: else if (episode_start)           fault_time <= timestamp_ms; / else if (fault_reg_read_done)     fault_time <= '0;
AIM.2.reason: When a host read lands on the clock a first cause appears in an empty fault_reg, fault_time takes timestamp_ms while fault_reg stays empty; if the cause was gone by the next clock, fault_time is left non-zero beside an empty fault_reg.

AIM.3.description: Episode start is detected from fault_reg having gone non-empty rather than from the capture conditions, so fault_time is latched one clock after the first cause
AIM.3.before: episode_start = convertor_running && (fault_reg == '0) / && (otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert / || window_trip || window_trip_SS);
AIM.3.reason: fault_time is still 0 on the clock fault_reg first shows a cause and takes the timestamp one clock later, which is the next millisecond's value when the first cause arrives on the clock before timestamp_ms increments.

AIM.4.description: The episode is judged empty by fault_time being zero instead of fault_reg being zero
AIM.4.reason: An episode that begins while timestamp_ms is 0 (the first millisecond after reset, or after the counter wraps) does not hold its start time: fault_time is overwritten with the later timestamp while any cause is still live after the counter moves on.

AIM.5.description: OVP is inferred against the recorded LATCH bit instead of the live latch_assert
AIM.5.reason: A CPLD-originated trip with latch_assert and latch_state both high and LATCH not yet recorded (the first clock, or after a host read) falsely sets the OVP bit, and a real analog OVP trip after an unread earlier CPLD trip is not recorded.

AIM.6.description: Over-temperature bypasses the capture gate: with otp_state high, causes are recorded even while the converter is stopped
AIM.6.reason: With ss_active and run_active both low, otp_state high sets the OTP bit (and any other live cause's bit, such as UVLO during power-down) in fault_reg where it should stay empty, with fault_time left at 0.

AIM.7.description: UVLO is recorded only in S_RUN; a UVLO that interrupts soft start is forgotten
AIM.7.reason: With ss_active high and uvlo_state asserted, the UVLO bit of fault_reg stays 0 while fault_time still latches a timestamp for an episode with no cause in it.

AIM.8.description: The clear-on-read leaves the OVP bit set; only the four lower cause bits are cleared
AIM.8.reason: After an inferred OVP has been recorded, a host read leaves fault_reg at 5'b10000 instead of 0, so every later read reports OVP until reset and later episodes never see an empty register to latch a new fault_time.

AIM.9.description: A host read clears only the recorded causes that have gone away; a recorded cause still asserted survives the read, even with the converter stopped
AIM.9.after: else if (fault_reg_read_done) begin /  / fault_reg <= fault_reg & {ovp, latch_assert, otp_state, uvlo_state, (window_trip || window_trip_SS)};
AIM.9.reason: With the converter stopped after a fault and the condition still present (UVLO still low, OTP still hot), a read leaves that bit set in fault_reg where the original returns to 0 and stays there because capture is gated off.

AIM.10.description: Causes are captured through a priority chain, one per clock, instead of independently accumulated
AIM.10.before: if(otp_state)                       fault_reg[BIT_OTP]   <= 1'b1; / if(uvlo_state)                      fault_reg[BIT_UVLO]  <= 1'b1; / if(window_trip || window_trip_SS)   fault_reg [BIT_OC]   <= 1'b1; / if(ovp)                             fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b1; / if(latch_assert)                    fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] <= 1'b1;
AIM.10.after: if(otp_state)                       fault_reg[BIT_OTP]   <= 1'b1; / else if(uvlo_state)                 fault_reg[BIT_UVLO]  <= 1'b1; / else if(window_trip || window_trip_SS) fault_reg [BIT_OC] <= 1'b1; / else if(ovp)                        fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b1; / else if(latch_assert)               fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] <= 1'b1;
AIM.10.reason: When two causes are live together while the converter is running (for example otp_state with uvlo_state, or window_trip with latch_assert), only the first in the chain is recorded and the other bit of fault_reg stays 0 for as long as the first remains asserted.

AIM.11.description: The OVERCURRENT bit follows the live window trips while running instead of being set and held
AIM.11.reason: If the window trip deasserts while ss_active or run_active is still high, bit 0 of fault_reg drops back to 0 before the host has read it, so a transient overcurrent is no longer reported.

AIM.12.description: A host read clears fault_reg only when the converter is stopped; a read during S_SS or S_RUN does not clear it
AIM.12.reason: Reading the register while ss_active or run_active is high leaves the earlier causes in fault_reg although the cause conditions are gone, while fault_time is cleared to 0, so the record keeps stale bits with no start time.

AIM.13.description: latch_assert also sets the OVERCURRENT bit, on the assumption that every CPLD latch trip is an overcurrent
AIM.13.reason: With latch_assert high and neither window trip asserted while the converter is running, fault_reg reads 5'b01001 instead of 5'b01000.

AIM.14.description: The episode start is detected only in S_RUN: a first cause captured during soft start does not latch fault_time
AIM.14.reason: With ss_active high and run_active low, a first cause sets its fault_reg bit but fault_time stays 0, and stays 0 for the rest of the episode because fault_reg is no longer empty.

AIM.15.description: OVP inference is suppressed while an overcurrent window trip is live, on the assumption that the latch trip then belongs to the overcurrent
AIM.15.reason: An analog trip (latch_state high, latch_assert low) that coincides with window_trip or window_trip_SS while running sets only the OVERCURRENT bit; fault_reg[4] is never set.

AIM.16.description: Recording LATCH_ASSERT withdraws an already recorded OVP bit, treating the two latch origins as mutually exclusive in the record
AIM.16.after: if(ovp)                             fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b1; / if(latch_assert) begin / fault_reg[BIT_LATCH] <= 1'b1; / fault_reg[BIT_OVP]   <= 1'b0; / end
AIM.16.reason: OVP captured first and latch_assert rising later in the same running episode leaves fault_reg with LATCH set and OVP cleared, although bits must only be cleared by a host read.

AIM.17.description: The record is judged empty from the four lower cause bits only; a recorded OVP does not count as an open episode
AIM.17.reason: In an episode whose only recorded cause is OVP, fault_time is re-latched on every clock a cause is live, so it follows timestamp_ms or jumps to the time of a later cause instead of holding the start time.

AIM.18.description: UVLO is recorded only as the first cause of an episode; a UVLO that follows another recorded cause is treated as a consequence and dropped
AIM.18.reason: With a cause already in fault_reg and the converter still running, uvlo_state going high no longer sets fault_reg[1].

AIM.19.description: LATCH_ASSERT is recorded only once the debounced SCR readback confirms it, not when the CPLD asserts the trip
AIM.19.reason: latch_assert high while latch_state is still low (the readback lags the trip) sets no LATCH bit; if running ends before latch_state rises, fault_reg[3] is never set, while fault_time is still latched for the episode.

AIM.20.description: fault_time is cleared by a host read only when the converter is stopped; a read during S_SS or S_RUN clears fault_reg but leaves the old start time
AIM.20.reason: After a read while running with no cause live, fault_reg reads 0 but fault_time keeps the previous episode's timestamp instead of returning to 0.

AIM.21.description: The three bytes of timestamp_ms are latched into fault_time in reversed order
AIM.21.reason: fault_time at the start of any episode differs from timestamp_ms whenever the top and bottom bytes of the timestamp are not equal.

AIM.22.description: fault_time is cleared when the converter stops, instead of being held until the host reads the record
AIM.22.after: else if (episode_start)           fault_time <= timestamp_ms; / else if (!convertor_running)      fault_time <= '0;
AIM.22.reason: Once ss_active and run_active both drop after a fault, fault_time returns to 0 while fault_reg still holds the causes, so the start time is lost before the host can read it.

AIM.23.description: OVP is inferred from any disagreement between latch_state and latch_assert, not only from the latch set without the CPLD's trip
AIM.23.reason: While running, latch_assert high before the debounced latch_state reads back sets the OVP bit as well as LATCH, reporting a CPLD-originated trip as an analog overvoltage.
